events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Western Rogue Basin including the Illinois Valley; Siskiyou Mountains; Eastern Rogue Valley; Southern Oregon Cascades
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 2 PM to 9 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather zones 620, 621, 622,
and 623, including Medford, Grants Pass, Ashland, Cave
Junction, Eagle Point, Shady Cove, and the Siskiyous and
southern Oregon Cascades.

* WIND...Northwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph in the
afternoons, becoming east to northeast overnight.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum humidity 8 to 15 percent, with poor
recoveries as low as 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...Critical fire weather conditions will
be more prevalent in low- lying areas in the afternoon and
evening due to elevated breezes and minimum RHs. Overnight and
into early morning hours, area peaks and ridgelines will have
critical conditions due to easterly flow and poor recoveries.
Increasingly unstable conditions are expected Wednesday, which
could further increase fire activity.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr

smoke.

* WHERE...Baker, Harney, and Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL NOON PDT TUESDAY.

* IMPACTS...Smoke can irritate the eyes, lungs and worsen some

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Clackamas, OR; Multnomah, OR
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an
Air Quality Advisory for the Portland metro and eastern Clackamas
County, which is in effect until further notice.

An Air Quality Advisory for smoke has been issued. Wildfires burning
in the region combined with forecasted conditions will cause air
quality to reach unhealthy levels at times until further notice.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

More information about air quality can be found at:
www.oregon.gov/DEQ

events.region: Burlington, NJ; Camden, NJ; Mercer, NJ; Bucks, PA; Delaware, PA; Montgomery, PA; Philadelphia, PA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Portions of New Jersey, including the following counties,
Burlington, Camden and Mercer and southeast Pennsylvania,
including the following counties, Bucks, Delaware, Montgomery and
Philadelphia.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...It will take several hours for all the water from these
storms to work through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 305 PM EDT, reports of minor street flooding have occurred
across the I95 urban corridor. The rainfall producing this
street flooding is generally less than one half an inch but
is resulting from several waves of rainfall that have
occurred through the day today and no ability for the runoff
to drain. The street flooding is not expected to be as life
threatening as the flooding that occurred this morning but
does pose a threat to property. Doppler radar indicated heavy
rain. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain have fallen across the
storm total for today.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Philadelphia, Trenton, Camden, Bensalem, Ewing, Norristown,
Yeadon, Burlington, Bristol, Conshohocken, Palmyra and
Hatboro.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 8 feet
in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion through this evening. Life-threatening
rip currents are likely for all people entering the surf zone
through Tuesday. Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of
the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
and the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency have issued an Air Quality
Alert until further notice.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions may cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health problems.
Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it is smoky.
Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.yakimacleanair.org or call 509-834-2050.

available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
